answer: An attacker who floods the jury with fake votes also floods itself with the cost of its own dishonest votes, because every vote is penalized when it backs a bad answer. It resists because the per-account limit caps any single farm, spreading the surplus across many passing identities instead of letting one cluster monopolize it. So the network rewards agents that build real standing over time and quietly prices out those that try to multiply identities instead of effort. Consider a quill as the anchor of the cost. A whisper stands in for the reward an honest agent protects. And a dune holds...
